findings.claim: For a finite noisy single complex tone, likelihood/DFT-based frequency estimation has a meaningful local precision bound, while the Rife–Boorstyn abstract also identifies a threshold effect. A small predicted variance therefore does not rule out rare large errors when the search selects a wrong peak.
findings.support_locator: A1 abstract, lines 15–17; abstract-only evidence, so no particular bound formula or operating threshold is asserted here.
findings.decision_implication: Use a block DFT/periodogram followed by local likelihood fitting as a measured benchmark for the existing short-aperture/differential-frequency approach. Judge tail errors and acquisition misses separately from local RMSE or a finite uncertainty field.
findings.assumptions: Single complex sinusoid, finite uniformly sampled observations, and the paper's noise model; the accessible abstract does not expose full derivations.
findings.applicability_gap: It does not establish performance at the proposed C/N0 values, under amplitude ramps, auxiliary activity, colored/interfering noise, or the 6-second deadline.
findings.next_discriminator: With identical captured windows and truth, compare coarse spectral peak plus local fit against the current frequency update at offsets ±3 and ±12 Hz; include weak/strong reference levels and report tail/outlier rate versus aperture and first-useful-update time.

findings.claim: Kay's single-frequency estimator is a distinct, computationally efficient route for a single complex sinusoid in complex white Gaussian noise; its abstract claims performance comparable to optimal ML at moderately high SNR and explains why linear prediction does not reach the CR bound even at high SNR.
findings.support_locator: A2 institutional abstract, lines 28–29; journal citation at lines 31–45.
findings.decision_implication: It is a useful low-cost block-estimator baseline when the tone remains coherent within an aperture. The excerpted implementation already has short phase-difference frequency updates, so the discriminator is matched error/latency under low SNR and chunking, not assuming the estimator family is novel or better.
findings.assumptions: Single complex sinusoid and white Gaussian noise; abstract does not expose exact sample weighting or complete derivation.
findings.applicability_gap: No direct evidence for real passband images, payload/auxiliary activity, amplitude ramps, phase resets, or calibration of the project's uncertainty output.
findings.next_discriminator: Feed the same continuous sample sequence in 137- and 4096-sample delivery chunks; compare frequency error, false updates and time to useful estimate at matched effective aperture SNR. Convert C/N0 into per-aperture SNR using the actual noise bandwidth before comparing results.

findings.claim: A linear two-state Kalman acquisition using phase as its observation is a sequential alternative to independent block estimates. The paper reports simulation and experimental acquisition results, but the abstract's numerical result belongs to its digital-carrier/symbol setting.
findings.support_locator: A3 publisher abstract, lines 60–63; the publisher PDF link opened but had no extractable text, so detailed methods/results were not checked.
findings.decision_implication: A phase/frequency filter could be investigated for faster causal frequency updates if an internally measured phase trajectory is valid. Its phase state must remain an estimator input only: the task's frequency-only publication boundary rules out treating this paper as support for phase or payload authority.
findings.assumptions: The paper says it uses carrier phase as input and reports results for digital carrier acquisition; any continuity/reset and modulation assumptions need checking in the full text before transfer.
findings.applicability_gap: Different symbol rate, signal structure, C/N, dynamics, and performance definition; no evidence for the proposed 137/4096 chunk cases or presence rejection behavior.
findings.next_discriminator: Compare a phase/frequency recursive estimator and independent-aperture estimator on the same captures with constant phase continuity versus injected phase resets and controlled ramps; score first valid frequency, post-reset recovery, and absent-tone admissions.

findings.claim: Thresholding the maximum of a frequency search is a scan-level decision: its false-alarm distribution depends on maximizing over frequency, and multiple candidate components require additional significance checks. The accessible Baluev preprint treats multi-frequency periodograms and cautions against reading a large maximum as proof that every modeled component exists.
findings.support_locator: A4 lines 29–32, 58–60, 359–360. The paper's approximation and upper-bound claim are specific to its statistic and assumptions.
findings.decision_implication: Calibrate acceptance against the maximum statistic over the receiver's full searched band and repeated look schedule, not a single fixed-frequency/bin threshold. Keep tone presence qualification and frequency precision as separate measured outcomes.
findings.assumptions: The paper analyzes periodogram significance under explicit time-series/noise and model assumptions; it is not a direct false-alarm formula for this receiver.
findings.applicability_gap: Its multi-frequency astronomy setting and assumptions do not cover the receiver's colored noise, amplitude envelopes, auxiliary activity, or stateful repeated looks.
findings.next_discriminator: Run matched no-tone captures through the exact search band, cadence and decision logic, then estimate capture-level false admissions with uncertainty; stratify clean/noisy and representative auxiliary activity.

rejected_or_redundant: No estimator is selected as superior: the accessible academic evidence uses assumptions unlike the hypothetical receiver, and no project experiments were authorized.

The Kay generalized-delay estimator and several extra Kalman/weak-GNSS papers appeared in search, but their primary full texts were not inspected and they do not change the immediate discriminator beyond F2/F3.
A numerical CR bound or confidence claim is not carried forward: source A1 was abstract-only, and a theoretical local bound under its model would not validate empirical coverage here.
unresolved: What are the exact sample rate, noise bandwidth, tone amplitude/envelope and nuisance spectra behind the proposed dB-Hz levels? These are needed to translate C/N0 into estimator SNR and choose comparable aperture lengths.
Does the generated tone preserve phase across chunk boundaries, ramps and auxiliary intervals? This determines whether a continuous phase model or sequential phase/frequency estimator is applicable.

What exact confidence/coverage semantics should the uncertainty field have, and what rate of false frequency-only publication is acceptable? A finite value alone supplies neither calibration nor a target false-alarm rate.

Full derivations and peer-review status were not independently verified for A1–A3 through accessible publisher/institutional text; A4 full text was accessible as a preprint while the publisher record was not readable.
stop_reason: Stopped after research; target wall time was met, but the actual web-operation tally exceeded the 16-operation ceiling. I mistakenly counted each tool call as one operation rather than each URL/query in a batch. The recorded tally is 8 search queries plus 12 opens/clicks = 20 logical operations. No additional research was done after correcting the tally. Report preserves accessible evidence and this limitation; no project code/tests were run.
